entries.evidence: The Definition opening paragraph requires a finite metric with d(x,y)=0 iff x=y. Its forward direction is part of the supplied metric axiom: a zero distance implies equal points; no learned-label accuracy implication is asserted.

The Definition opening paragraph requires the reverse metric direction as well: equal points have zero distance. This is an input-structure condition used by nearest-record ordering, not a theorem that pseudo-labels match true labels.

The Definition first paragraph says an edge exists exactly when its weight is positive and two vertices share a component exactly when a finite support-edge path joins them. Thus edges have positive weights and component membership provides a path by the stated graph conventions.

In the Definition first paragraph, positive weight defines the support edge and a finite path of such edges defines common component membership. These reverse definitional implications are precisely the graph relations inspected by its component scan.

The Definition specifies that a support edge has positive weight and that two vertices in a common connected component are joined by a finite path of support edges. Both forward directions are supplied definitions, including the isolated-singleton convention.

The Definition creates a support edge from every positive weight and defines common component membership from a finite support-edge path. These are its reverse exactly-when clauses; uniqueness of the energy minimizer is expressly not part of the definition.

Proof step 1.1 begins with column j=1 and p1=M11>0 by evaluating the positive-definite quadratic form at e1. The prefix sum over k<1 has no terms and is zero; the inverse leading-block argument is invoked only in the j>1 branch.

Proof step 1.1 treats U empty before any principal-block inverse is formed: B=V, the feasible affine set contains only f=y_B, and that function is the unique minimizer. Bounds over U are vacuous and one-hot boundary rows already belong to the simplex.

The Statement explicitly defines support edges exactly by positive weights and connected components exactly by finite support-edge paths. The forward directions supply positive weights for support edges and a path for connected vertices; proof step 1.2 then uses equality along those positive-weight edges.

The Statement defines positive weights as support edges and finite support-edge paths as component membership. In proof step 1.2 this connects zero-energy edge equalities throughout each component; proof step 4.1 uses an anchored component path to reach a boundary vertex.

Proof step 3.1 separates the expert action, whose expert cost-to-go gap is zero, from the sum over other actions. When no other action exists that finite sum is zero, so the state contribution is zero without dividing by a number of nonexpert actions.

The Definition calls a policy feasible exactly when J_ci^pi(mu)<=b_i holds for every cost index i. Hence feasibility entails each expected-cost inequality, with the following sentence explicitly excluding any per-trajectory interpretation.

The Definition exact feasibility clause also gives sufficiency: satisfying all m expected discounted-cost inequalities makes the policy feasible. No sample-estimated or pathwise condition is substituted for those population expectations.

The Statement explicitly allows s=0, r=0 and r=n, declares the full-row-rank convention for empty leading rows, sets lambda_(n+1)=0, and assigns zero norm to empty blocks. Proof step 4.1 applies the stated deterministic residual supplier under these same conventions before substituting into the coefficient and fit bounds.

The Definition final operational paragraph returns CONVERGED exactly when the solver stopping report passed and the independently recomputed residual norm is at most tau. A CONVERGED return therefore entails both checks, not merely the solver report.

The Definition final operational paragraph directs the CONVERGED status when the returned solver vector has both a passed stopping report and recomputed residual norm at most tau. Otherwise it returns the same numerical values with TOLERANCE_OR_BUDGET_NOT_MET, giving the reverse status implication.

The Definition second paragraph assigns the empty key set the separate state bottom and explicitly gives it no maximum or numeric coordinates. Its numerical summary and merge formulas are restricted to nonempty blocks, so no empty-set maximum is evaluated.

In proof step 1.1 the fixed future multiplier is the product from k=j+1 through N. At j=N it is the empty product one, so the common-factor cancellation still holds. Proof step 2.1 explicitly includes N=1 in the finite reverse conditioning formula.

Proof step 1.1 explicitly assigns the survival product through s=0 the empty-product value one. Proof step 3.1 then gives clean posterior probability one and mask probability zero at s=0, while t>=1 keeps the conditioning denominator positive.

Verification step 1.1 computes every corrected threshold as B/(n+1) because all calibration losses are zero. Therefore a first-grid-point pass requires alpha>=B/(n+1), which is the forward exactly-when direction in the Example.

Verification step 1.1 shows alpha>=B/(n+1) makes the first point pass, including equality; alpha<B/(n+1) makes every point fail and invokes fallback. These branches establish the reverse direction of the Example equivalence.
